review.publication: Local only. No commit, push or deployment.
review.scope: Forest types, tree foliage classes and vegetation; separate broadleaf from deciduous and remove false forest/subtype exclusions.
review.attribution: Reviewed adaptations of Open English WordNet 2025 by the Open English WordNet Team, derived from Princeton WordNet; CC BY 4.0 and Princeton notices remain in docs/quality/2026-10-09-q11.md#sources-and-reuse. NPS, US Forest Service and Gramota entries independently check botanical and lexical distinctions. Definitions are not copied verbatim; Russian wording, scope restrictions and graph mappings are editorial adaptations.
review.context_policy: All new concepts and assertions use U1 with unspecified strength. Existing home contexts and relation grammar remain unchanged. Forest families describe dominant vegetation, not purity, fixed stand percentages or legal land-use thresholds.

sense_decisions.scope: A tree that seasonally sheds its foliage. This includes some conifers and is not identical to broadleaf tree.
A tree that retains green foliage throughout the year. Restrict evergreen plant to trees; this does not mean individual leaves never fall.
The intersection of coniferous tree and seasonally deciduous tree. Larch demonstrates that the intersection is nonempty.
The intersection of coniferous tree and evergreen tree, without claiming that all conifers are evergreen.
The intersection of broadleaf tree and seasonally deciduous tree.
The intersection of broadleaf tree and evergreen tree. Leaf form does not require seasonal leaf loss.
A forest whose characteristic dominant trees are conifers. It need not be evergreen or consist exclusively of conifers.
A forest characterized by broadleaf trees, with seasonal leaf retention left open.
A forest characterized by seasonally deciduous trees. Broaden the dictionary broadleaf-only wording to admit deciduous conifer forest.
A forest characterized by trees retaining green foliage through the year; not every plant or leaf must be evergreen.
Select the mixture of coniferous and broadleaf trees. Do not assert both dominance-class genera merely from the presence of both components.
A forest associated with abundant rainfall. Do not restrict the term to tropical forests or import a universal numerical rainfall threshold.
A forest of the tropical climatic region. Some tropical forests are seasonally dry, so this is not a synonym of rainforest.
A forest of the temperate climatic region, without requiring broadleaf or deciduous dominance.
A rainforest in the tropical climatic region.
A rainforest in the temperate climatic region; Pacific Northwest forests provide a counterexample to rainforest being necessarily tropical.
A coniferous forest characterized by evergreen trees.
A coniferous forest characterized by seasonally deciduous trees such as larches.
A broadleaf forest characterized by seasonally deciduous trees.
A broadleaf forest characterized by evergreen trees.
A forest characterized by pine trees. The family does not require a pure single-species stand.
A forest characterized by spruce trees; retain the tree sense rather than spruce wood.
A forest characterized by true fir trees, genus Abies.
A forest characterized by larch trees; this provides an explicit deciduous/coniferous forest intersection.
A small wooded area characterized by birch trees. This is neither an individual birch nor a timber substance.
The plants collectively present in a region. Exclude botanical science, plant-growth processes, inactivity and medical homonyms; do not classify a collection as one plant.
The collective plant life of a forest, distinct from forest as a wooded area.
Select the shrub layer below the forest canopy. Restrict broad English undergrowth to the woody shrub layer denoted by the Russian forestry term; do not import every fern, herb or young canopy tree.
Oak includes both evergreen and deciduous species. Preserve its broadleaf genus without adding a universal deciduous parent.
Taiga is not made coextensive with every boreal-biome use, nor forced beneath evergreen coniferous forest. Preserve its existing broad forest genus.
Reject universal forest/jungle disjointness, but defer the full Russian jungle/thicket and region scope.
Do not import the orchard/garden sense or treat a grove as necessarily cultivated.
The existing wooden/tree terminology and reversed root/branch/leaf assertions require a separate material/part-whole review; this batch does not certify them.

review.limits: No fixed canopy, area, rainfall, latitude or dominance thresholds. Broadleaf, foliage retention and climatic region are distinct classifications. Existing forest material percentages, broad plant/root/leaf assertions, wood-versus-tree terms and the full jungle/biome/ecosystem scope remain separate review tasks. No universal exclusion is asserted between forest dominance classes. No application test suites.

exclusion_review.decision: Reject the two false forest/subtype exclusions while preserving their genus rows. Also reject forest/jungle universal exclusion based on the reviewed forest sense of jungle. Other exclusions remain unchanged.

review.collision_decision: Move the sole colliding English label deciduous tree off the broadleaf-tree record 249 to the new seasonal-foliage record. No other collision is accepted.

refreshed_comparison.caveat: Normalized spelling candidates are not verified identities or missing-concept counts.

remove_terms.reason: Move the seasonal foliage meaning to its own record. Deciduous conifers such as larches are not broadleaf trees.

repairs.reason: The tree sense of larch belongs to the deciduous conifers. Its original tree genus remains an ancestor. OEWN 2025: oewn-11639312-n. Source: https://www.nps.gov/noca/learn/nature/treesandshrubs.htm
The selected true-fir tree of genus Abies is an evergreen conifer; exclude fir timber and Douglas-fir homonyms. OEWN 2025: oewn-11641124-n.
Taiga in the selected forest sense is within forest, so it cannot be disjoint from its genus. Preserve the original accepted genus.  Source: https://research.fs.usda.gov/treesearch/64446

A grove is a small wooded area within the existing broad forest sense, not an excluded peer of forest. Preserve its genus. OEWN 2025: oewn-08455920-n. Source: https://gramota.ru/poisk?mode=slovari&query=%D1%80%D0%BE%D1%89%D0%B0
Jungle and forest are not universally disjoint: the dictionary forest sense of jungle is a counterexample. Do not force all broader jungle/thicket usages beneath forest. OEWN 2025: oewn-08456014-n.
